rows.summary: The web platform of Dragonfly: single-page apps written in Nuclear with the same words as the mobile platform.
body: The web platform of Dragonfly: single-page apps written in Nuclear with the same words as the mobile platform. Its dialect `react` (React 19, React Router, Vite, Vitest) and its TypeScript runtime `dragonfly-web`.
This repository is a folder of the NuclearLang working tree (`nuclear/dragonfly-web`); the platform's rules are the
working tree's `../AGENTS.md` ([nuclear](https://github.com/nuclearlang/nuclear/blob/main/AGENTS.md)) and its state is `../STATUS.md`.

rows.title: Dragonfly for web — the platform and its dialect `react` — Dialect `react`
rows.summary: Dialect `react`
body: | Path | What it does |

| `dialects/web/react/dialect.toml` | kinds, decorators, `[architecture]`, `[project]` (`output = "build/app"`, `assets = ["public"]`), `[toolchain]`, `[call_site.Log]`, defs list, auto_imports of the runtime |

| `dialects/web/react/templates/` | kind templates; `dragonfly_g.tpl` → `src/dragonfly.g.ts` (startDragonfly, dragonflyConfig, registerModels, registerDragonfly, routes, appRouter); `index_ts.tpl`, `index_html.tpl`, `package_json.tpl`, `tsconfig.tpl`, `vite_config.tpl` |
| `dialects/web/react/docs.toml` | editor docs of every kind and decorator (required by a test) |

| `packages/dragonfly-web/src/` | runtime: `result`, `errors`, `inject`, `config`, `app`, `http` (Repository, Decode, Cache), `state`, `react` (views, Providers, hooks), `html`, `events`, `session` (SessionManager, Acl, Guards, NetworkManager), `router`, `log`, `testing` (entry `dragonfly-web/testing`) |
| `packages/dragonfly-web/test/runtime.test.ts` | 7 vitest tests (repository, cache, mocks, states, views, events) |
| `examples/examples-web/characters/` | the complete example (golden `examples/expected/characters`): list and detail screens, state, tests |
| `tools/react-check/check.sh` | runtime tsc, example built, tsc --strict, vitest (4 tests), vite build, runtime tests |

rows.title: Dragonfly for web — the platform and its dialect `react` — Dialect `react`
rows.summary: `dialects/web/react/` (extends `typescript`): React 19 without JSX, React Router 7, Vite 7, Vitest 4 + jsdom + Testing Library.
body: `dialects/web/react/` (extends `typescript`): React 19 without JSX, React Router 7, Vite 7, Vitest 4 + jsdom +
Testing Library. Views are classes (`StatelessView` / `StatefulView`) shown through `createElement`
(`statelessOf` / `statefulOf`), so hooks work in `build` and a stateful keeps its fields; a state model generates
`<Model>Builder`; `@screen(providers)` wraps the screen in `Providers` and `this.manager(X)` reads a provided manager
(`[decorators.provide]`). Two generic emitter rules came with it: `[kinds.<k>.syntax] construct` (a call to a
declaration of that kind, here a function call instead of `new`) and named arguments to a `named_params` kind kept
as one object in a dialect with `named_args = "object"`.

rows.title: Dragonfly for web — the platform and its dialect `react`
rows.summary: Future repository `dragonfly-web` (ADR-0093).
body: Future repository `dragonfly-web` (ADR-0093). Decisions: ADR-0097 (the web platform is the mobile platform in a
browser; first dialect `react`; the analysis of zustand / TanStack Query / react-hook-form for later steps).
**The platform** (`spec/web.md`, Nuclear only): the mobile kinds that make sense in a browser, with the same words:
views (`stateless`, `stateful` with `build() Element`), `appConfig`/`config`, `repository` (http), `usecase`,
`appcomponent`, `service`, `aggregate`, state models + `statemanager`, `@screen`, `event` + `component` with `@on`,
`guard`, `tests`. Contract: `dialects/web/platform.toml`. Not yet: forms, converters, translations, local database,
plugins, AI.

rows.title: AGENTS.md — NuclearLang
rows.summary: This project is written in NuclearLang (`.nuc`), dialect `react`.
body: This project is written in NuclearLang (`.nuc`), dialect `react`. Its syntax is not TypeScript, Dart nor Python.
- Before writing code, read the sheet: `nuclear spec --brief --dialect react`.
- After each change: `nuclear check <file>.nuc --dialect react --json` must report no errors; fix exactly what each error says (most carry a `fix`).
- Look up instead of guessing: an API `nuclear defs show <Name> --dialect react`; a kind or decorator
`nuclear help <word> --dialect react` (all: `nuclear help words --dialect react`); a topic `nuclear help <topic>`.
- Never edit generated code (`build/` and the `.ts`/`.dart`/`.py` built from the `.nuc`): change the `.nuc` files.
<!-- /nuclearlang -->

rows.title: NuclearLang website — Build
rows.summary: (cd tools && npm install) # markdown-it, shiki and smol-toml, once node tools/content.mjs # the content, from the tree site.toml names ([source] tree; NUCLEAR_TREE overrides it) dragonfly build # the app into build/app (public/ copied) dragonfly install # npm install in build/app dragonfly test #…
body: ```sh
(cd tools && npm install)        # markdown-it, shiki and smol-toml, once
node tools/content.mjs           # the content, from the tree site.toml names ([source] tree; NUCLEAR_TREE overrides it)
dragonfly build                  # the app into build/app (public/ copied)
dragonfly install                # npm install in build/app
dragonfly test                   # vitest: the tests of test/
dragonfly run                    # vite dev, http://localhost:5173
(cd build/app && npx vite build) # the published site in build/app/dist
`tools/content.mjs` renders every page's markdown with the code already highlighted (shiki, with the Nuclear grammar
of the editors and their Chernobyl theme), so the browser receives HTML and never parses markdown. The home page's
sample is transpiled to TypeScript, Dart and Python by the installed `nuclear` when the site is built. For search
engines and agents that read without JavaScript, every page also has a plain HTML copy in `/static/` (and the
sitemap, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`).
The addresses are the paths of the repositories' files: `/docs/language/01-syntax` is `docs/language/01-syntax.md`.
A link between pages reloads the page (the content is cached by the browser); navigation by address inside the app is
a later step of the web platform.

rows.title: NuclearLang website
rows.summary: The NuclearLang site, written in Nuclear with Dragonfly's web platform (dialect `react`): its screens, state managers, search and content repository are `.nuc` files.
body: The NuclearLang site, written in **Nuclear** with Dragonfly's web platform (dialect `react`): its screens, state
managers, search and content repository are `.nuc` files. The content is the documentation of the `nuclearlang`
repositories (`docs/`, `spec/` of `nuclear`, `dragonfly-mobile`, `dragonfly-backend`, `dragonfly-web`), turned into
JSON by a build script; the app only reads it.

rows.title: Website
rows.summary: Its own repository, `website` (today `~/Documents/projects/nuc/react/nuclearlang_website`; ADR-0083): only the site, written in Nuclear with Dragonfly web (react); the content stays with the code it documents.
body: Its own repository, `website` (today `~/Documents/projects/nuc/react/nuclearlang_website`; ADR-0083): only the site, written in Nuclear with
Dragonfly web (react); the content stays with the code it documents. Its README has the details.
- `site.toml` holds every text, menu, link and address of the site (ADR-0101); the side menu lists pages by path or
`*` pattern of the source tree.
- `tools/content.mjs` reads the `.md` files of the source roots (`nuclear`, `dragonfly-*`), skipping
`[source] internal` (`docs/aprende/`, `docs/context/`), and writes `public/content/` (pages as JSON with shiki
highlighting, `site.json`, `home.json`, the search index), `/static/` plain pages, `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt`
(ADR-0088), the sitemap, and copies `tools/release/install.sh` / `install.ps1` to the root.
- A new dialect or framework feature gets its user guide (a `.md` in its repository) and, if it is a new area, a
line in `site.toml`'s sidebar.
- Language: English (ADR-0082). Deploy (GitHub Pages, SPA fallback) is pending (STATUS.md).
